metrics.main_line: task: feature|bugfix|refactor|debug|docs|review|test|research|plan|ops|chat (the kind of work asked for)
brief: clear|partial|vague (how complete the request was)
level: easy|normal|hard (how hard the work was)
shift: new|build|grew|redo|fix, only if it applies (a new unrelated task; building on the last one; the scope grew; redoing earlier work; fixing a fault in it)
size: xs|s|m|l|xl (how big the work was)

metrics.sub_line: result: done|partial|blocked (done = the agent finished what its brief asked; partial = some of it; blocked = it could not go on, such as a missing file, tool or permission)

retry: none|model|brief|tools|scope|other (is this run a second try at what an earlier run listed below was meant to deliver, because that run fell short? none = no, or there is no earlier run; model = it needed a stronger model; brief = the earlier brief was too vague or lacked something; tools = the earlier agent lacked a tool or a permission; scope = the task was cut too wide or changed; other)

metrics.main_line: missing: files,goal,constraints,done,repro,scope or none (what the request lacked that you had to find or guess; a comma list)
plan: none|made|following|deviated (no plan; you wrote one; you worked to one; you departed from it)
skill: helped|unneeded|would-help|none (whether a skill you ran helped; would-help:<name> if one of the listed skills would have)
found: yes|partial|no (for research or search work: whether you found what was asked)

metrics.sub_line: fit: smaller|right|larger (smaller = a smaller, cheaper model could plainly have done this: simple lookups or mechanical edits; right = it suited the model it ran on; larger = the agent struggled in a way a stronger model would not have)

brief: clear|partial|vague (how complete the brief was: clear = what to do and what to hand back; partial = the goal without the details; vague = neither); missing: files,goal,scope,done or none (what the brief lacked that the agent had to find or guess; a comma list)

metrics.main_line: prior: needed|some|none (how much of the earlier conversation this work needed)
check: targeted|full|build|run|manual|none (how you verified the change)

metrics.tool_note: That tool result was large. Add out=needed|part|unneeded (how much of it you needed) to the tag that ends your final reply.

metrics.main_extra:
The first time in this session you finish a piece of work the user asked for, add this before your tag, after a blank line, and never again after that:

metrics.main_extra_untagged:
The first time in this session you finish a piece of work the user asked for, end your reply with this, after a blank line, and never again after that:

text.intro: The user turned on ClaudeGlass metrics capture, to see where their tokens go. If you are a subagent, ignore this note.
text.main_tag_intro: End your final reply to each user message with one line, [cg: key=word ...], using only these keys and words:
text.sub_tag_intro: End your final report with one line, {tag}, using only these words:
text.skip_key_line: Leave out a key you can't judge.

judge.intro: You label one exchange between a user and Claude, an AI coding assistant, for the user's own usage analytics. You get an excerpt of it: the user's message, what Claude did, and the end of Claude's final reply. Answer with one line and nothing else, [cg: key=word ...], using only these keys and words. In them, "you" means Claude:
judge.rule: Judge only from the excerpt: a plan, skill or check it doesn't show wasn't there. Give every key that applies. Leave one out only when it doesn't fit this work (found outside research or a search; shift on a first message) or the excerpt can't tell at all.

lines.task: task: feature|bugfix|refactor|debug|docs|review|test|research|plan|ops|chat (the kind of work asked for: docs = documentation or comments only; ops = CI, build, deploy or configuration; test = tests only; research = finding something out; review = judging existing work; debug = finding a fault's cause; chat = no work asked for)
lines.brief: brief: clear|partial|vague (how complete the request was: clear = what to change and what done looks like; partial = the goal without the details; vague = neither)
lines.shift: shift: new|build|grew|redo|fix, only after an earlier message (new = an unrelated task; build = a next step on top of the last task; grew = more asked of the same task; redo = the same task done another way; fix = fixing a fault in the last work)
lines.size: size: xs|s|m|l|xl (how big the work was: xs = a line or two, or only an answer; s = a small change; m = a feature with its tests; l = many files; xl = a large change)
lines.plan: plan: none|made|following|deviated (none = no plan; made = Claude wrote one this turn, as a plan file or as steps in its reply; following = Claude carried out one written earlier; deviated = Claude departed from one written earlier)
lines.prior: prior: needed|some|none (how much the work relied on the earlier conversation: needed = the message only makes sense with it; some = it helped; none = a fresh request)
lines.check: check: targeted|full|build|run|manual|none (how Claude verified its change: targeted = ran the tests for the part changed; full = ran the whole test suite; build = only built or type-checked; run = ran the program itself to see it work; manual = only read it back; none = no check, or nothing changed)

agent.intro: You label one finished run of an AI coding agent, for the user's own usage analytics. You get an excerpt of it: the brief the agent was given, what it did, the end of its report and the session's earlier agent runs. Answer with one line and nothing else, [cg: key=word ...], using only these keys and words:
agent.rule: Judge only from the excerpt. Give every key; leave one out only when the excerpt can't tell at all.

text.cold_return:
Write the tip on this note's last line, word for word, at the end of your reply, after a blank line and before any tag. The user came back to this session after a break. Handle the message exactly as you would have without this note: it changes nothing about the work.
> **ClaudeGlass tip:** The prompt cache expired while this session sat idle for {idle}, so this reply wrote about {ctx} tokens of context again{compacted}. If you came back only to see whether the work is done, the last reply or the task panel already says. For new work, running /clear first skips the rewrite.
text.status_poll:
Write the tip on this note's last line, word for word, at the end of your reply, after a blank line and before any tag. The user is asking about work that is still running in the background. Handle the message exactly as you would have without this note: it changes nothing about the work.
> **ClaudeGlass tip:** Asking how it's going while work runs in the background makes Claude read the whole session, about {ctx} tokens, to say little that is new. {poll_how}
text.drip_feed:
Write the tip on this note's last line, word for word, at the end of your reply, after a blank line and before any tag. The user has sent {count} small change requests in a row, one message each. Handle the message exactly as you would have without this note: it changes nothing about the work.
> **ClaudeGlass tip:** That's {count} small changes in a row, each its own message, and each one re-reads the whole session, about {ctx} tokens. Working out everything the work still needs and sending it as one message gets it done in one pass, for fewer tokens.
text.plan_first:
Write the tip on this note's last line, word for word, at the end of your reply, after a blank line and before any tag. The user's message asks for about {steps} separate changes, outside plan mode. Handle the message exactly as you would have without this note: it changes nothing about the work.
> **ClaudeGlass tip:** That's a job of about {steps} separate changes, sent outside plan mode. Plan mode agrees the approach before anything changes. {plan_how}
text.big_paste:
If most of the user's message is a log, a file or command output, write the tip on this note's last line, word for word, at the end of your reply, after a blank line and before any tag. Otherwise don't mention this note.
> **ClaudeGlass tip:** Your message is about {tokens} tokens, and every later reply reads it again. Pasting only the part that matters, or saving the rest to a file and giving the path, costs less.
text.quiet_output: That result was about {tokens} tokens, and every later reply reads it again. Next time, {how}.
text.plan_fresh:
Write the tip on this note's last line, word for word, before you start building. Then carry on unless the user stops you.
> **ClaudeGlass tip:** This plan was approved with about {kept} tokens of planning in the session, and every reply of the build reads them again. Building it in a fresh session would carry about {kept} fewer tokens on each reply. {fresh_how}
text.plan_fresh_early:
Write the tip on this note's last line, word for word, as the last line of the plan you submit for approval. If this reply doesn't end in a plan, add it to the plan you submit later. Handle the message exactly as you would have without this note: it changes nothing about the work.
> **ClaudeGlass tip:** Approve with clear context: this session holds about {kept} tokens of planning chat, and every reply of the build would read it again. {clear_how}
